text:
sahil: Heads-up — we started seeing slow persistent memory creep on the streaming/chat toolloop runs in prod-rw-2 this morning. Sessions that stream >70k tokens steadily grow ~1.2GB over 30m until restart. Repro-able on my local toolloop harness with the same model config.
anya: ugh. regressing or a new workload? did this start after any particular deploy?
mike: last prod deploy was an infra change around kernel selection heuristics for quantized models (PR #4582) — landed yesterday evening.
sahil: It looks correlated. I've run the local long-run for 45m and captured heap profiles. Early signal: a lot of small slab allocations pinned in the KV cache arena. Not typical: entries aren't getting freed even after eviction passes.
elaine: can you paste the pprof flame or a small diff? also, do cache eviction logs show evict attempts?
sahil: pasted a small excerpt below (pprof top). The hot allocs are in kv_prefix_slot_ref and page_fragment_alloc pathways.

```
Showing top 20 nodes
1.2GB  1.2GB  runtime.malloc
900MB  900MB  kv.page_fragment_alloc
400MB  400MB  kv.prefix_slot_ref
... 
```

mike: that's pointing at fragmentation — too many tiny fragments and our coalescer isn't merging them. Could be the new kernel selection changed alignment expectations so fragments are no longer coalescible.
anya: i checked eviction logs around the repro run — evict loop ran, returned candidates, but reclaim only freed ~3% of candidates. logs show repeated: `candidate->busy=true` followed by `skip_reclaim()`.
sahil: that matches: entries marked for eviction but still referenced by active streaming sessions (toolloop hook refs). The weird part is refs seem to be short-lived in codepaths but linger in slot ref counts. suspect a refcount edge where prefix cache increments but doesn't decrement on short-lived continuation paths.
elaine: can you share the minimal repro command? i'll run it in staging with extra tracing.
sahil: repro: `./toolloop_run --model rwd-v1-small --stream --session-steps 10000 --kv-backend=pmem --trace-evict=1 --heap-pprof=1` — I ran that twice. attaching short trace snippet: 

```
[12:01:15] evict_loop: candidate_id=4234 state=marked
[12:01:15] reclaim: found refcnt=1 (expected 0) prefix_ref++ at prefix_cache_mark()
[12:01:15] reclaim: skip_reclaim candidate_id=4234 reason=busy
[12:01:16] prefix_cache_insert: slot=4234 flags=PINNED
[12:01:16] prefix_cache_unshard: returning without dec ref (early return path)
```

mike: early-return path leaving the ref incremented — that smells like the batching heuristics fast-path. We recently added fast-path in `process_batch()` to reduce latency for common-case short batches. Might be skipping cleanup on error/timeout.
anya: timeline: fast-path landed in PR #4519 (two days before PR #4582). PR #4582 then toggled a kernel fallback that increased fast-path hit rate for long seq lengths. combo could expose leak.
elaine: i'm booting a staging instance with both PRs reverted to isolate. also enabling `kv.debug_evict=true` so we can see full lifecycle.
infra-bot: deploy queued: staging/rw-v2 revert-4519-4582 (by elaine). ETA 6m.
sahil: in parallel i'll add an assert in prefix_cache_unshard() to log stack trace when refcount>0 on supposed free path. if we get traces, we can map callsites to fast-path.
mike: good. if confirmed, fix likely is to add a guarded decrement on all early-return paths in process_batch(), and add a unit test exercising the error/timeout fast-path under streaming toolloop. also consider making eviction mark stronger (defer pin operations) until finalize.
anya: action items: (1) elaine revert & repro in staging (2) sahil add assert+pprof dumps every 60s (3) mike prepare fix PR for fast-path ref cleanup + unit test (4) add eviction diagnostic to CI that runs a 15m longstream smoke to catch regressions.
sahil: noted. adding a quick mitigation: increase eviction aggressiveness and force full coalescer sweep (`kv.coalesce_force=1`) for the cluster to slow memory growth while we debug. Not ideal but buys time.
elaine: staging repro started, initial heap snap shows same pattern. will post pprof link when available. :eyes:
mike: thanks. if we get a stack trace from assert, tag me. I can instrument the runtime to auto-decrement on destructor paths as a short-term patch.
anya: great triage. please keep notes here so oncall handover has context.
sahil: will do — will paste pprof links and final root cause once we have stack traces. :thumbsup:
